# Detection coverage (generated)

<!-- Generated by `python -m agentwall.src.bench --format markdown`; do not edit by hand. A test fails if this file differs from a fresh run. -->

Corpus `1eef50813cce3eaa`: 2312 labelled samples written by the RedHand team, in English and Bahasa Malaysia. Detectors measured: `egress_guardrail`, `radar`, `radar_model`, `manifest_auditor`, `description_auditor`.

**How to read this.** The corpus is small and written by us, so these numbers flatter the detectors: real attackers rephrase, and variants of one idea are correlated (see the families column). The 95% intervals show how uncertain a rate is at this size. Nothing here means RedHand blocks 100% of anything, and RedHand only checks what flows through its gateway.

Status rules (fixed in advance): **covered** = detection >= 90% and false alarms <= 1%; **partial** = >= 50% and <= 5%; **weak** = detects something but misses the partial bar; **not covered** = detects nothing. A category with fewer than 20 samples on either side is **insufficient data**.

## Held-out results (never tuned on: quote these)

Held-out samples are not used to write or tune rules (a change made after seeing them is disclosed where it happens). A held-out set written by the same author as the rules is less independent than one written by someone else, and 20 samples can only prove so much: read the confidence interval, not the point estimate. A category with a held-out set is rated on it; the dev table above is what the rules were written against.

| Category | OWASP | Malicious | Benign | Detection (95% CI) | False alarms (95% CI) | Hard benign false alarms | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `injection_indirect` | LLM01 | 28 | 32 | 24/28 = 86% (69%-94%) | 0/32 (at most 11% with 95% confidence) | 0/10 | **partial** |
| `output_path` | LLM05 | 20 | 20 | 19/20 = 95% (76%-99%) | 0/20 (at most 16% with 95% confidence) | 0/10 | **covered** |
| `output_ssrf` | LLM05 | 20 | 20 | 20/20 (at least 84% with 95% confidence) | 0/20 (at most 16% with 95% confidence) | 0/10 | **covered** |
| `output_xss` | LLM05 | 20 | 20 | 20/20 (at least 84% with 95% confidence) | 0/20 (at most 16% with 95% confidence) | 0/10 | **covered** |
| `tool_poisoning` | LLM01 | 20 | 20 | 13/20 = 65% (43%-82%) | 0/20 (at most 16% with 95% confidence) | 0/12 | **partial** |

Status is assigned from point estimates, by rules fixed in M1. With 20 benign samples the false alarm rate is only known to be below about 16%, so read **covered** here as "no misses found yet", not as a guarantee. The corpus grows with independently written samples (plan `docs/plans/phase4-m4-plan.md`, section 11.3) and the status rule moves to the upper confidence bound at M4.6.

## Ready to block? (the block gate)

Block mode does not exist: SQL, core and the gateway all refuse it. This table says whether the measured evidence would be enough to ever offer it. It reads only the frozen blind rounds above, never our own held-out samples, and a change to the rules file makes old rounds stale (rules fingerprint `21d583301e041d02`). Rules: **G1** Independent evidence: A frozen test round written by someone other than the rule author, scored once. **G2** Measured on these rules: That round was scored on exactly the rules that run now (same fingerprint, helper model off). **G3** False alarms low enough: The 95% upper bound of false alarms is at most 3%, with at least 40 harmless samples built to look like attacks. **G4** Catches enough: The 95% lower bound of attacks found is at least 50%. **G5** Tested on long, realistic text: At least 40 harmless samples are 2 KiB or longer (pages, emails, documents).

| Check | Evidence | G1 | G2 | G3 | G4 | G5 | Eligible |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hidden instructions in tool answers | round3 | pass | **fail** | **fail** | **fail** | **fail** | no |
| Script and active markup | round2 | pass | **fail** | **fail** | pass | **fail** | no |
| Internal and cloud-metadata addresses | round2 | pass | **fail** | **fail** | pass | **fail** | no |
| Sensitive file paths | round2 | pass | **fail** | **fail** | pass | **fail** | no |

- **Hidden instructions in tool answers:** The rules changed after this round was scored. It needs a new round. False alarms: 10 of 146 harmless samples, 95% upper bound 12.1% (limit 3.0%); 48 built to look like attacks (need 40). Even with no false alarm, at least 125 harmless samples are needed. Attacks found: 34 of 94, 95% lower bound 27.2% (need at least 50.0%). Long harmless samples (2 KiB or more): 0 (need 40). Real tool answers are pages and documents; the samples we have are short.
- **Script and active markup:** The rules changed after this round was scored. It needs a new round. - **Internal and cloud-metadata addresses:** The rules changed after this round was scored. It needs a new round. Long harmless samples (2 KiB or more): 0 (need 40). Real tool answers are pages and documents; the samples we have are short.
- **Sensitive file paths:** The rules changed after this round was scored. It needs a new round. ## Known gaps (read these first)

- Hidden instructions are found about 4 times in 10 on text the rules have not seen, with about 7 to 8 false alarms per 100 harmless documents.
- On real long documents the checks flag more than on our short samples: 10 of 10 real web pages raised a script flag, and on 186 strangers' READMEs the hidden-instruction check flagged 12% and the risky-output check 6% (a recorded measurement, not blind evidence: docs/security/real-document-replay.md).
- A rephrased or politely worded attack, and an attack buried in the middle of a long document, are often missed.
- Malay hidden-instruction detection found 4 of 25 attacks in the independent round; Indonesian attacks were not measured; Chinese is not covered.
- Documentation, runbooks and security write-ups that quote attacks cause false alarms.
- The helper model for hidden instructions is off: on unseen text it added almost nothing at its current settings.
- Secret leaks and MCP manifest risks have small sample sets (20 each) and are weak or partial.
- The Radar only sees what flows through the RedHand gateway. It never blocks: block mode does not exist until a measured gate is passed.
